name: emit
description: Decides the next bead-action changeset deterministically. Pure function over the impact report, the task journal, the spec directory, and a caller-supplied git HEAD SHA. Emits changeset.json — an ordered, tool-agnostic list of create and close operations, drawn from the wider label/create/close/tag vocabulary, with forward-reference encoding — that an external adapter consumes.

requirements.title: Pure function over inputs
requirements.description: spex emit reads the impact report (stdin or --impact), the task journal, the spec directory, and the --git-head SHA; writes changeset.json to stdout. No subprocess invocations, no live tracker calls, no git calls. Given identical inputs, always produces byte-identical changeset output. The invocation itself is a declared external surface — the api `spex emit`, provided by EmitCommand — and the declared name is the bare invocation, so the flags listed here sit behind it: adding, renaming or dropping one moves no name and is invisible to the diff. Nothing that reaches this function can carry an api node either, because an api produces no impact action, so no changeset op ever names one.

requirements.title: Topological ordering within type levels
requirements.description: Ops are emitted in an order that respects type tiers (proposal epic first, then features and data_flow tasks, then multi-component test tasks) and respects spec-graph dependencies within each tier. When new bead B depends on new bead A, A's create op comes before B's, so the adapter can build A first and forward-resolve B's dep at exec time. Same-tier ties break deterministically by spec_node_id.

requirements.title: Priority propagation through project requirements
requirements.description: Each create op carries a priority derived from the chain component.implements → module_requirement.preq_id → project_requirement.priority. Lowest numeric priority wins across the implements set. Passed through in the op's priority field for the adapter to forward to the tracker.

requirements.title: Parent resolution from mapping store
requirements.description: Each create op's parent field encodes the proposal epic for the run. The epic is either the op_id of a same-run epic create (first op) or a bead_id ref to a pre-existing epic, recognised by folding the task journal for the proposal's slug. All non-epic creates in the run parent under this single epic reference. The title's store is identity-bearing legacy; the journal fold is the source.

requirements.title: Forward-reference encoding for in-batch creates
requirements.description: Parent and dependency fields use two ref shapes: {"ref":"bead","bead_id":"<id>"} for a task the journal fold already pairs with the spec node; {"ref":"op","op_id":"<id>"} for the result of another create op in the same changeset. Resolving DepSpecNodeIDs from impact into these two shapes is how emit fixes the broken-dep-graph bug: same-run deps become op refs resolved by the adapter at exec time rather than pre-resolved stale bead IDs. Version 2 dropped the third ref:spec_node shape and its adapter-time lookup against the mapping store: a dep that is neither in-batch nor in the fold is an emit error at emit time instead.

requirements.title: Idempotency label construction
requirements.description: Each create op carries an idempotency.label field taken from the op itself: a fresh or modify-pair create's label is spex:<spec_node_id> — the node's identity hash, stable across the modify lineage because the hash does not change — a cleanup create's label is spex:cleanup-<spec_node_id>, and an epic create's label is spex:<proposal-slug>. No counter, no cursor, no store read: the label is a pure function of the op. The adapter matches the label against the tracker before creating; a pre-existing match produces a was_existing=true receipt rather than a duplicate bead.

requirements.title: Git HEAD threaded from caller
requirements.description: emit accepts --git-head <sha> and embeds the SHA into changeset.json under the top-level git_head field. The adapter uses this value to build commit:<HEAD> labels on obsoleted beads. spex never calls git rev-parse; the caller supplies $(git rev-parse HEAD) from their shell.

requirements.title: Deterministic changeset schema
requirements.description: changeset.json carries a top-level "version": 2 field. Version 2 removed ref:spec_node from the adapter-facing vocabulary: emit resolves those refs in-process from the journal fold, so an op's deps reach the adapter as ref:op or ref:bead only. The schema is stable across runs: op ordering is deterministic, all ref shapes use named fields, field order is canonical so two runs with identical inputs produce byte-identical output suitable for git diff review.

requirements.title: Tool-agnostic operation vocabulary
requirements.description: Operations are label, create, close, and tag — abstract over any bead tracker. No tracker-specific flags or subcommand names appear in changeset.json. Adapters for br, bd, GitHub Issues, or Jira consume the same vocabulary.

components.name: ChangesetBuilder
components.description: Composes changeset.json from the impact report, the task journal's fold, the spec graph, and caller-supplied git HEAD. Delegates dep resolution to Resolver, op ordering to TopologicalSorter, and idempotency labels to IdempotencyLabeler. Writes the final v2 changeset with canonical field order.

components.name: Resolver
components.description: Resolves each create action's DepSpecNodeIDs and parent_spec_node_id into refs the adapter can apply blind. Classifies each dep: if another op in the same batch targets the spec_node_id → ref:op; otherwise the journal fold answers with the open task already tracking the node → ref:bead. There is no adapter-time fallback: a dep that is neither in-batch nor in the fold is an emit error, because the adapter no longer reads any spex-owned file. Also computes priority by walking component.implements → module_requirement.preq_id → project_requirement.priority and taking the minimum.

components.name: TopologicalSorter
components.description: Orders the create ops so every in-batch dep comes before its dependent. Uses Kahn's algorithm over the (create op, DepSpecNodeIDs → op_id) DAG restricted to the current batch. Detects cycles and returns an error (a cycle in spec-graph deps within one batch is a spec error, not an emit error). Secondary sort key: spec_node_id lex order, for determinism on unconstrained pairs.

components.name: IdempotencyLabeler
components.description: Assigns each create op its idempotency.label, branching on action class: spex:<spec_node_id> for fresh and modify-pair creates — the same value in both cases, because the label is the node's own identity hash — spex:cleanup-<spec_node_id> for cleanup creates, spex:<proposal-slug> for epic creates. Stateless: no cursor, no store dependency, nothing persisted; the label is read off the op.

components.name: EmitCommand
components.description: CLI entry point: spex emit --proposal <ref> --git-head <sha> [--impact <file>] [--out <file>]. Reads the impact report (stdin or --impact), folds the task journal at <spec-dir>/.history.jsonl via the map module, loads the spec graph, wires ChangesetBuilder, writes changeset.json to stdout or --out.

data_flows.name: Emit flow
data_flows.description: Emit's place in the run and its internals. Position: emit is the fourth of six stages — spex validate gates, spex diff and spex impact --beads produce the impact report, emit turns it into changeset.json, the adapter executes that and writes receipts.json, and spex ingest reconciles the pair; every hand-off from diff onwards goes through a file, so each stage can be re-run from the artifact its predecessor wrote, and a partial run leaves the snapshot untouched so the next diff recomputes from the same baseline. Internals: impact report + the task journal fold + spec graph + git HEAD → TopologicalSorter orders ops → IdempotencyLabeler assigns labels → Resolver classifies each create's refs → ChangesetBuilder composes and writes changeset.json v2.

apis.name: spex emit
apis.description: Emit a tool-agnostic changeset from an impact report
